model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity on normalized core earnings (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation is already expensed inside core earnings (the stream valued here); equity-settled option expense is immaterial (CSV StockBasedComp 0-2m FY2023-25). SBC path held explicitly at 0% so it is not charged twice; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Model flows in CAD (IFRS reporting currency). Quote is the NYSE line MFC in USD because the folder's price refresh reads the bare symbol MFC from Yahoo in USD. fx_rate 0.7019 CAD->USD = 1/1.4247 (Yahoo CAD=X, 2026-10-03T21:00Z). Parity check: TSX MFC.TO C$61.31 at 2026-10-02T20:00Z / 1.4247 = US$43.03 vs NYSE US$42.93, a 0.2% gap (close-time/FX-print difference). CAD per-share values = USD values / 0.7019.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,677m common shares outstanding at 31-Dec-2025 (FY2025 MD&A) plus ~3m dilutive options (FY2025 diluted vs basic EPS) = 1,680m. Held flat: the FY2026 NCIB (up to 42m shares) is funded out of the FY2026 FCFE in the flows, so lowering the count for H1-2026 repurchases would double-count them. No Q2-2026 interim filing is extracted; the Q2-26 count is roughly 1,650-1,655m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.0% in CAD: Government of Canada 10y ~3.3% + beta ~1.15 x 5.5% ERP ~ 9.6%, rounded up for the legacy US LTC tail and Asia geopolitical exposure. Same rate in all three scenarios (risk charged once via scenario paths and weights). Stream is post-interest, post-preferred FCFE so it is discounted at the cost of equity and net debt is held at zero.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not separately modelled: leases are inside core expenses, so inside the earnings stream; no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Core earnings are shareholders' earnings (excludes participating policyholders and NCI) and the stream is after preferred share and LRCN distributions (C$321m in FY2025), so preferred/other equity (C$6,660m) and NCI are NOT deducted again in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: SKILL.md routes insurers to BVPS compounding x exit P/B. Overridden to FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, following the folder's life-insurer precedents (PRU, GL, IAG.AX, and BMO for the CAD-filer/USD-quote shape), because (1) IFRS 17 restated FY2022 equity from 56,061 to 46,876 and net income from +7,294 to -1,933, leaving only three comparable book-value years, and (2) IFRS book excludes the CSM (C$38.27 adjusted BVPS vs C$25.91 BVPS), so BVPS compounding understates the capital-light Asia/WAM growth. The distributable flow (remittances funding dividends + buybacks) is what accrues to common holders. ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = core earnings available to common shareholders (post-tax, after preferred/other equity distributions), FY2025 C$7,200m (FY2025 MD&A non-GAAP reconciliation). 'ebitda_margin' = normalization of core to owner earnings: core has exceeded net income attributed to common by C$1.8-1.9bn in each of FY2024-25, of which ~C$0.97bn/yr is ALDA (real estate/PE/timber) underperformance against the long-term return assumptions embedded in core; base haircut 8% (~C$580m) charges roughly 60% of that recurring ALDA shortfall, treating market-experience items as mean-reverting. 'cash_tax_rate' = 0 because the stream is already post-tax (GMT included in core from 2025). 'capex_pct' = capital retained to fund growth (LICAT required capital, new-business strain, bolt-on M&A), as % of core; FY2025 actual common distributions were C$5.4bn (dividends ~C$2.98bn + buybacks C$2.43bn) = 75% of core, consistent with management's C$22bn+ 2024-27 remittance target; base retention 26% fading to 17% (= terminal g 3% / ~17.5% ROE, applied to normalized earnings). D&A and SBC 0 (inside core). Buybacks: active repurchaser, 1,729m -> 1,677m shares in FY2025; buybacks are value-neutral here (they are a use of the FCFE). Excess capital above internal LICAT targets is NOT added to the bridge (conservative; upside in the bull narrative). FY2022 IFRS 17 break: no growth rate or ROE trend in this file bridges the IFRS 4 FY2022 row to IFRS 17 years except where labelled 'mixed basis'.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.3% IFRS 17 basis FY2022R->FY2025) is far below EPS CAGR (8.5%): Manulife distributes ~75% of core earnings (dividends + C$2.4-3.3bn/yr buybacks), and FX/ALDA marks hit book. Equity growth is therefore not the business growth rate; EPS on the IFRS 17 basis is selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: revenue_3yr_cagr is IFRS 17 insurance revenue FY2022R 23,118 -> FY2025 28,888 (total revenue is fair-value noise and not comparable across the IFRS 17 break, so no 5yr figure). eps_3yr_cagr = diluted EPS FY2023 2.61 -> FY2025 3.07 (only two years exist on the IFRS 17 basis; FY2022 restated EPS is negative). eps_5yr_cagr and equity_5yr_cagr are MIXED BASIS (FY2020 IFRS 4 -> FY2025 IFRS 17) and shown for completeness only. equity_3yr_cagr uses the IFRS 17 restated FY2022 total shareholders' and other equity 46,876 -> 50,121; from the 1-Jan-2022 restated opening 45,355 the 4yr CAGR is 2.5%. FCF CAGRs are null: insurer operating cash flow is policyholder-asset noise, not owner cash. Core EPS grew 10% (FY2024) and 8% (FY2025, 3.85 -> 4.21); Q2-2026 core EPS +16%.

base.narrative: SANITY FIX 2026-10-04: aggregate core earnings to common +7% in FY2026-27 (was 9%), between FY2025's actual +4.8% (6,871 -> 7,200) and H1-26's ~+12% CER, fading to 3.5%. ALDA shortfall persists at ~C$580m/yr. Retention 26% of core early (~74% distributable, matching FY2025 actual 75% and the C$22bn remittance target), fading to 17% at terminal.

bull.narrative: SANITY FIX 2026-10-04: growth trimmed from 12/11/10 to 10/10/9 in the early years. Core ROE reaches 18%+; Asia compounds at high-teens and hits 50% of core; WAM private-credit (Comvest) and Indonesia scale; ALDA returns recover to assumption so the haircut shrinks to 4%; LTC de-risking releases capital so retention is lower.

bear.narrative: US in-force experience (LTC morbidity, annuity lapse) stays adverse, ALDA marks keep running ~C$1bn below assumptions (15% haircut), Hong Kong/mainland China sales slow on geopolitics, and a stronger CAD shrinks translated Asia/US earnings; more capital retained to defend LICAT.

scenario_narratives.base: Manulife delivers close to its medium-term plan: Asia (38% of segment core earnings, +18% FY2025, +21% Q2-26) and Global WAM (+14%) carry growth while Canada grows low-single-digit and the US in-force book is flat-to-down. Core earnings to common grow ~7% for two years (FY2025 actual +4.8% aggregate; Q2-26 +12% CER) and fade to 3.5% by year 10. Recurring ALDA underperformance (~C$1bn/yr in FY2024 and FY2025) is treated as partly structural: 8% of core is haircut every year. About three-quarters of core is distributed through dividends (35-45% payout target) and the NCIB; retention fades as growth slows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 18%+ core ROE target is hit and held: Asia bancassurance (DBS, Chinabank to 2039) and agency keep compounding at mid-to-high teens, India JV and Dubai HNW add optionality, WAM private credit scales, and the Munich Re LTC deal (closing Q4-2026; 24% cumulative LTC risk reduction) plus prior RGA/Global Atlantic deals free capital for larger buybacks. ALDA marks normalize so core converts more fully to earnings (4% haircut).
scenario_narratives.bear: The legacy US LTC/VA book produces another reserve or experience hit (US core fell 30% in FY2025), ALDA marks stay ~C$1bn/yr below assumption, Hong Kong mainland-visitor sales and broader Asia slow on trade/geopolitical tension, and CAD strength cuts translated earnings. Core growth slows to ~4% and fades to 2.5%, 15% of core never reaches book, and more capital is retained to hold LICAT near 130%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default) because multi-decade LTC/VA liabilities and ALDA marks have repeatedly produced below-core charges, and the Asia growth engine carries China/HK geopolitical exposure. Base 50%: H1-2026 is running ahead of plan (core EPS +16%, core ROE 16.3%), with LICAT 136% and a Moody's Aa3 upgrade. Bull 25% (below the 35% default) because it needs the ROE target, continued Asia compounding and ALDA normalization to all happen together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the distributable flow to common shareholders (core earnings available to common, haircut for recurring ALDA underperformance, less capital retained for growth) at a CAD cost of equity of 10%. Debt, preferreds/LRCNs and NCI are already charged inside the stream, so nothing is deducted afterwards. IFRS book value is not the compounding base because IFRS 17 broke the history in FY2022 and book excludes the CSM.
valuation_philosophy.warning: Sanity check tripped on implied P/E (13.0x vs 10yr avg 6.3x) and P/B (1.44x vs 10yr max 0.87x). One fix pass applied: base and bull near-term growth trimmed (base 9% -> 7% aggregate core earnings growth), because FY2025 aggregate core growth was only 4.8% and 8.45% EPS growth rests on two post-IFRS 17 years. Result: weighted IV US$40.95 -> US$38.13 (C$58.34 -> C$54.32); P/E cleared (13.0x -> 11.8x, under 2x avg); P/B still trips (1.44x -> 1.31x) and that residual is left unresolved on purpose. The check's history divides dividend-adjusted USD prices by CAD per-share figures, and its pre-2023 book is pre-IFRS 17. On that basis today's market price is itself ~14x, above the 13.9x 'max'. In CAD on unadjusted closes, MFC has traded at ~15-20x GAAP EPS and 1.7-2.4x IFRS 17 common book since FY2024. No exit P/B cap (0.43/0.59/0.87x) was imposed: on that basis it would value MFC at roughly US$13-19, 55-70% below a price the market has paid for two years. No CoE premium was added either: 10% CAD is already above the ~9.5% CAPM build, and the scenario weights charge the LTC/regulatory risk once (25% bear).
adjustments_made: Base growth path 9,9,8,8,7,6,5,4.5,4,3.5 -> 7,7,6.5,6,5.5,5,4.5,4,3.5,3.5 (aggregate core earnings to common)
Unchanged: cost of equity 10.0%, terminal growth, ALDA haircuts, retention paths, weights 25/50/25, bear path
key_risks_to_valuation: Core earnings is a management non-GAAP measure: it has exceeded net income to common by C$1.8-1.9bn a year in FY2024-25. The normalization haircut (4-15% by scenario) is the single most consequential judgment here.
Retention rate: if growth requires more retained capital than ~25% of core (new-business strain, LICAT changes, M&A), distributable FCFE falls one-for-one.
Legacy US LTC morbidity and longevity assumptions: a reserve strengthening hits book and buyback capacity.
FX: CAD-reported, with USD/HKD/JPY earnings; also, the USD quote moves with CAD/USD independently of the CAD value.
Share count is the 31-Dec-2025 figure; no Q2-2026 interim filing has been extracted, so balance-sheet anchors are about nine months old.

CoE (10%), exit/terminal mechanics, haircuts, retention and weights unchanged. No exit P/B cap: the check's historical P/B (0.43-0.87x) divides dividend-adjusted USD closes by CAD book incl. pre-IFRS 17 equity, so today's market price itself reads 1.44x on that basis.
